title: ReviewPlane live-view channel, version 1
description: Single source for the version 1 live-frame channel of docs/API.md section 18.2: the metadata, quality-adaptation and heartbeat messages exchanged over /ws/v1/browser-sessions/:sessionId/live, and over the internal worker-to-control-plane leg that feeds it. The binary frame payload is a separate transport message referenced by the live.frame metadata that precedes it and is deliberately not a JSON schema: base64 in JSON would inflate bandwidth and blur the separation section 18.2 requires. TypeScript models, validators and canonical encoders are generated from this file. Hand-maintained equivalents in apps/server, apps/browser-worker or apps/web are a review failure.

channels.stream: Frame metadata and the scheduler's applied quality.
channels.control: Attachment, viewer quality requests, session state and refusals.
channels.keepalive: Liveness and observed stream statistics in both directions.

live.attached.description: First message on an accepted viewer connection. It is sent only after authentication and project authorisation have both succeeded, so a refused viewer never sees one (docs/SECURITY.md section 7).

live.frame.description: Metadata for exactly one frame. The binary payload follows as the next transport message and is never embedded here (docs/API.md section 18.2). Produced by the worker's scheduler and relayed unchanged by the control plane.

live.quality.description: The quality and rate the worker scheduler decided to apply. The scheduler is authoritative: this message reports a decision, it does not confirm a request.

live.quality_request.description: A viewer's advisory request for a mode or rate, relayed by the control plane to the worker. The worker may honour, bound or ignore it (docs/API.md section 18.2).

live.heartbeat.description: Periodic liveness plus the observed send, drop and buffer figures, so a viewer can display the drop rate docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 6.3 requires to be measurable.

live.viewer_heartbeat.description: Viewer liveness and the last frame it actually rendered, which is how the control plane detects a slow viewer before its send buffer grows.

live.session_state.description: Browser-session status, URL and viewport at attachment and on every change, so the page can state the session's condition as text rather than by the presence of frames.

live.error.description: A refusal or stream failure, carrying both the stable error class and the failure state the UI must show (docs/UX_FLOWS.md section 18).

frame_too_large.description: The encoded message exceeded its byte bound. Detected on the raw bytes before deserialisation.

malformed_json.description: The message was not well-formed JSON, or was truncated.

unsupported_protocol_version.description: protocol_version was absent, not an integer, or not a version this build accepts.

unknown_message_type.description: type was absent or not a version 1 message type. Unknown types are rejected, never ignored.

payload_too_large.description: The payload exceeded the byte bound declared for its message type.

schema_violation.description: The message parsed but did not satisfy the schema for its message type.

frame_rate_bands.description: The two rates docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 6.3 fixes, expressed as the inclusive frames-per-second bounds the scheduler adapts within. session_room is 10 to 20; thumbnail is 2 to 5. A scheduler that leaves its band is a defect, not an adaptation.

transport_records.description: Record kinds of the internal worker-to-control-plane leg, which carries the same messages over a length-prefixed byte stream rather than a WebSocket: 1 is a JSON message bounded by max_live_message_bytes, 2 is a binary frame payload bounded by max_frame_payload_bytes. On the viewer leg the same separation is a text WebSocket message followed by a binary one.

identifier.description: Opaque durable identifier (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 3). Consumers MUST treat the value as opaque: the schema bounds only its length and character class and never its documented prefix.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC, with a mandatory trailing Z.

resolved_url.description: Absolute URL observed by the browser. Page-derived and therefore untrusted (ADR-0010): bounded in length and character class, rendered as text, never executed.

reason_text.description: Short operator-facing explanation. Never carries page content verbatim beyond its bound, and never carries credentials (docs/SECURITY.md section 18).

message_type.description: Version 1 message type. Unknown types are rejected, never ignored. This enumeration MUST equal the keys of x-protocol.messages.

error_class.description: Stable error class, drawn from the docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 12 enumeration so a refusal reaches the viewer with the same code the HTTP API would report. This enumeration MUST equal x-protocol.error_classes.

live_mode.description: Which of the two rates of docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 6.3 the stream is running at. session_room adapts between 10 and 20 frames per second; thumbnail between 2 and 5.

frame_format.description: Media type of the binary frame payload. JPEG only: live frames are transient viewing data, not evidence, and lossless originals are the business of an explicitly captured screenshot (ADR-0009).

frame_retention.description: Retention applied to the binary payloads of this stream. The single value is the point: docs/SECURITY.md section 14 sets live_frames: never and ADR-0009 forbids a recording path here, so a stream cannot advertise anything else.

session_status.description: Browser-session lifecycle status (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 12), reported so the page states the session's condition as text.

failure_state.description: The actionable state docs/UX_FLOWS.md section 18 requires the UI to show instead of a blank canvas or a generic error. Each value names a cause a human can act on.

quality_reason.description: Why the scheduler chose the quality it did. Recorded so an operator can tell an adaptation from a defect.

viewport.description: Browser viewport in CSS pixels plus device pixel ratio (docs/API.md section 11). The frame payload's own dimensions are reported per frame and may be smaller after an adaptation.

device_scale_factor.description: Device pixel ratio of the browser session.

envelope.description: Live-channel message envelope. Every message names the browser session it concerns and the stream instance it belongs to, so a message from a superseded stream is recognisable rather than merely late.

protocol_version.description: Protocol version. Stage 0 accepts 1 only; any other value is rejected with PROTOCOL_UNSUPPORTED and is never best-effort parsed.

message_id.description: Sender-assigned message identifier, conventionally prefixed msg_.

type.description: Version 1 message type. Unknown types are rejected.

sent_at.description: Time the sender emitted the message.

browser_session_id.description: Browser session the message concerns, conventionally prefixed brs_. Absent only on a viewer message sent before attachment completes.

stream_id.description: Live-stream instance, conventionally prefixed lvs_. A new producer run gets a new value, so a viewer can discard frames belonging to a stream it no longer follows.

payload.description: Message payload. Its schema is selected by type. The message is bounded by x-protocol.limits.max_live_message_bytes and each payload by its own x-max-bytes.

x-requires.detail: every server message that describes a running stream names both the session and the stream instance
frame metadata is bound to its browser session so a relayed frame cannot be attributed to another

stream_attached.description: Confirms an authenticated, authorised viewer attachment and states the terms of the stream.

project_id.description: Project owning the browser session. The viewer was authorised against this value before this message was sent.

mode.description: Rate band the stream starts in.

format.description: Media type every binary frame payload on this stream will carry.

retention.description: Retention applied to frame payloads. Always never (ADR-0009, docs/SECURITY.md section 14).

max_frame_bytes.description: Largest binary payload the control plane will forward. A larger frame is dropped by the producer rather than truncated.

frame_metadata.description: Describes the binary payload that follows it as the next transport message. Nothing here is page-derived except by dimension, and the payload itself is rendered as an image and never as markup (ADR-0010).

sequence.description: Monotonically increasing per-stream frame number. Gaps are the dropped frames docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 6.3 prefers to a growing queue, and are therefore expected rather than exceptional.

captured_at.description: When the worker captured the frame.

mode.description: Rate band in force when the frame was captured.

width.description: Payload width in device pixels. It may be below the viewport width after a bandwidth adaptation.

quality.description: Encoder quality the frame was produced at, 1 to 100.

byte_length.description: Byte length of the binary payload that follows. A receiver that reads a different length MUST discard the frame rather than render a partial one.

dropped_before.description: Frames the producer discarded since the previous delivered frame. Reported per frame so the drop rate is observable without a separate metrics path.

quality_state.description: The scheduler's applied decision. The worker is authoritative over every field here (docs/API.md section 18.2).

target_fps.description: Frames per second the producer is now aiming for. It stays inside the band of x-protocol.vocabularies.frame_rate_bands for the mode.

quality.description: Encoder quality now in force, 1 to 100.

max_width.description: Largest payload width the producer will now emit.

max_height.description: Largest payload height the producer will now emit.

quality_request.description: A viewer's advisory request. The worker scheduler may honour it, bound it or ignore it; a viewer MUST NOT assume its request was applied and MUST read the live.quality that follows.

mode.description: Rate band the viewer would like.

max_fps.description: Upper rate the viewer can consume. A viewer may lower its own ceiling; it cannot raise the band's.

max_width.description: Largest payload width the viewer can usefully display, for example its rendered canvas width.

max_height.description: Largest payload height the viewer can usefully display.

requested_at.description: When the viewer made the request.

stream_heartbeat.description: Liveness plus the figures docs/TESTING.md section 12 requires to be measurable: delivered frames, dropped frames, and the depth of the bounded buffer that produced the drops.

frames_sent.description: Frames delivered to this viewer since attachment.

frames_dropped.description: Frames discarded rather than queued since attachment.

buffer_depth.description: Frames currently waiting to be written to this viewer.

buffer_capacity.description: Bound on that buffer. It is a fixed small number: a viewer that falls behind sees fewer, newer frames rather than a backlog.

measured_fps.description: Frames per second actually delivered over the last sampling window.

viewer_heartbeat.description: Viewer liveness and progress. The last rendered sequence is what lets the control plane distinguish a viewer that is slow from a link that is idle.

observed_at.description: When the viewer sampled its own state.

last_sequence_rendered.description: Sequence of the last frame the viewer actually painted.

session_state.description: Browser-session condition, sent at attachment and whenever it changes. The URL is page-derived and is rendered as text only.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the browser session.

url.description: URL the browser last settled on, when one is known. Untrusted content (ADR-0010).

control_epoch.description: Control epoch current at the browser session (ADR-0007). Reported so a later takeover surface has the value it must present.

live_capture.description: Whether frame capture is running. False with an otherwise healthy status is the degraded case docs/DEVELOPMENT.md section 11 requires: the session stays usable for navigation and screenshots without live frames.

live_error.description: A refusal or a stream failure. It carries the stable error class for logs and the failure state for the UI, because docs/UX_FLOWS.md section 18 forbids a generic message where a specific cause exists.

state.description: Actionable failure state the viewer must display.

message.description: Operator-facing explanation. Carries no credentials and no unbounded page content.

retryable.description: Whether reconnecting could succeed. A viewer MUST NOT reconnect in a loop when this is false.

retry_after_ms.description: Hint for how long to wait before reconnecting, returned with RATE_LIMITED (docs/API.md section 19).
